requirements.text: The Libra Scheduler will manage sequential and embarrassingly parallel batch jobs to be run on a homogenous Linux cluster.
The scheduler will enforce resource allocations according to user-centric priorities.
The scheduler will be dynamic, allowing for the reallocation of resources based on user priority and system load.
The scheduler will be scalable, ensuring performance does not degrade with the addition of nodes and jobs.
The scheduler will be configurable to allow for various scheduling policies that incorporate QoS parameters.
The scheduler will provide administrative security.
The scheduler will provide at least a basic level of job accounting.
The scheduler will use the proportional stride-scheduling algorithm to ensure resource allocation reflects job share.
The scheduler will support job submission with parameters including budget, deadline, and execution time.
The scheduler will allow users to query the cluster for current cost per unit time.
The scheduler will allow users to monitor the status of submitted jobs.
The scheduler will allow users to cancel their own submitted jobs.
The scheduler will allow users to check their credit balance.
The scheduler will allow users to check their usage history.
The administrator will be able to check the status of each node of the cluster.
The administrator will be able to check the usage pattern history of the cluster.
The administrator will be able to check the status of all submitted jobs.
The administrator will be able to check the load on each node of the cluster.
The administrator will be able to alter the cost structure of the cluster.
The administrator will be able to alter the scheduling policy of the cluster.
The administrator will be able to cancel, suspend, and resume any job.
The maximum response time for the submission of a job will be 1 minute.
The scheduler will ensure all jobs are completed with a 10% error allowance regarding deadlines.
The maximum cost payable as submitted by the user will be the maximum cost charged to the user.
The scheduler must implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to ensure only authorized administrators can modify scheduling policies, cost structures, or manage jobs belonging to other users.
The scheduler shall maintain a response time of under 1 minute for job submission and scheduling decisions when the cluster load reaches 500 concurrent jobs across 50 nodes.
The software shall achieve 90% code coverage via unit tests and pass all regression tests for the stride-scheduling algorithm before deployment.
The scheduler shall maintain a scheduling decision latency of less than 500ms for a cluster size of up to 100 nodes and a concurrent job queue of 10,000 jobs.
The scheduler shall ensure that 99% of all jobs complete within 110% of their requested deadline.

OPEN: The PRD mentions user authentication (User Id and Password) but lacks requirements for secure credential handling or communication. - All user authentication credentials and administrative commands must be transmitted over encrypted channels (e.g., SSH or TLS) to prevent credential interception.

OPEN: The PRD lacks requirements for audit logging of administrative actions. - The system must maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, including changes to cost structures, scheduling policies, and job status modifications, with timestamps and user identifiers.

OPEN: The failure handling strategy for the scheduler itself (the master node) is undefined. - The scheduler shall implement a checkpointing mechanism for its internal state to allow recovery within 5 minutes in the event of a master node failure.

OPEN: The PRD assumes the SGE cluster management system handles process migration, but does not define the failure behavior if a migration fails. - The scheduler shall detect failed process migrations and re-queue the job with an 'error' status, notifying the administrator and the job owner.

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'maximum number of jobs schedulable is limited only by the capacity of the nodes', but lacks a defined maximum throughput or concurrent job limit for the scheduler itself. - The scheduler shall support a minimum throughput of 50 job submissions per second without exceeding 80% CPU utilization on the master node.
